settings.d: None: No synchronization. Vertical Sync: Synchronize on video sync, avoids video tearing at the price of high visual latency. Adaptive Sync: Synchronize on video sync, except for late frames (below target FPS), also features higher visual latency. Frame Pacing: pace the frame rendering to limit visual latency, comes with the risk of introducing more stutters if the computer is not powerful enough.
settings.why: none, vertical sync, adaptive sync or frame pacing: adaptive sync draws as vertical sync, SDL having no adaptive mode; with nothing set, ours stays fastest, tearing allowed, at most 240 frames a second

settings.d: -1 will limit FPS to the display refresh rate 0 will not limit the display refresh rate Other values will limit the FPS to it (energy saving/less heat, framerate stability)

settings.d: Maximum number of 'frames in flight' (frames pushed to the GPU queue waiting for rendering). Higher values may lead to higher FPS, but at higher input latency. Recommended to be adjusted to the lowest value that allows a stable framerate. (Not supported in OpenGL version)
